correctness.rationale: Inspected Virbalas 2026 full primary text: equations (8)–(10) and the succeeding two-distinct-factor proof are established BEFORE the final independent congruence k≡0 (mod b−1) (Section 3 pp. 21–24). Covering primes have ord_b>1 and remain coprime to b−1; prescribed residues are units, and 1+b^M mod b^(M+1) is a unit. Replacing only the independent last residue with k≡2 (mod b−1) preserves every covering congruence, makes gcd(k,k−1,k+1,b−1)=1 in the required individual senses iff b is even and 3∤(b−1), and CRT produces a reduced fixed progression. The published proof then gives two distinct prime factors for both signs at each n>=1 once k>b^M. If b odd, only possible prime k=2, while 3|(b−1) forces only possible prime k=3; hence no infinite exceptions. Prime number theorem for fixed reduced progressions gives relative lower density >=1/phi(Q); Shiu gives arbitrary consecutive-prime strings, Maynard 2016 Theorem 3.3 positive starting-prime proportion for fixed h,Q. Independently enumerated the local residue feasibility for 208 bases; NOT a verification of infinitely many coverings or of prime distribution.

originality.rationale: The submitted contribution is the exact final claim after crediting the stated established inputs; best-of-knowledge originality is supported by matched statement/implication comparisons, not just title matches. A sharp base dichotomy for prime Brier coefficients resolves a substantial natural question about simultaneous covering systems and the interaction of local obstructions with global prime distribution. The reduced-progression refinement materially strengthens an existing all-bases composite-coefficient theorem; fixed-h consecutive primes and quantitative positive proportion are useful outcomes, not mere restatements of CRT.
